title: Stat efficiency and diminishing returns
summary: Aion Research Lab attribution, conditional KR values, and Double Chance examples.
qualifiers: Source recommendations, first-person statements, and testing claims are Kanon’s. Figures are captured examples rather than universal costs or ideal builds.
Captured source update: 9/20/2026. Regional and unconfirmed details remain qualified as written.

Efficiency values assume an ideal KR end-game build at the start of Season 1, level 50 and Lava Heart armor, including support buffs. Global launch, future KR, class buffs and diminishing returns can change these values.

content.text: This chapter will include a full breakdown of how all the stats work including detailed formulas. Some of these equations are not known to anyone yet and are becoming public for the first time with this doc.

I want to give a special shoutout to a well-recognized Korean Youtuber “Aion Research Lab” and his friends for discovering a lot of the formulas and equations listed out in this section. I spent a lot of time discussing numbers with him and it is STILL a work in progress…understandably so, considering the amount of sheer stats and convolution Aion 2 is with Damage.

Updates will be made on any new discoveries including fixes, but until then this is the most accurate up-to-date info we have on how all the stats work. I’ve tried my best to lay this out in the easiest to understand way while preserving the details.
Kanon credits Aion Research Lab and his friends for these equations and describes the work as ongoing. First-person discovery and testing claims below remain attributed to that source.

The following shows the damage efficiency for offensive stats based on current end-game Korea (on an ideal build) which is currently at the start of Season 1 (Start of level 50 and Lava Heart armor introduction). These stats also incorporate support buffs.

Generally speaking, diminishing returns are a thing. This means the values below will be different for Global launch (as well as future KR since more stats are added) considering we will have less stats, therefore less diminishing return impact. There will be a greater discrepancy with some stats for global launch. For example, Front/Back Damage Boost starts at a base value of 0% vs Critical Damage starting at 50%. The first 10% added to both stats favor Front/Back Damage Boost due to diminishing returns.
Also keep in mind certain classes have access to some buffs which diminish the value of certain stats the more you stack them (for example, the Critical Damage Boost stat with Gladiator).

content.text: Power Shards are consumables you equip that enhance your damage by a % value. Power Shards have slight diminishing returns from the PVE Attack bucket. The damage increase efficiency comes out to:
(Yellow) Superior Power Shard = 8.9% more damage (4.05% more than Regulars)

The raw tooltip bonuses are 5% and 10%, whereas the source estimates effective increases of 4.65% and 8.9%. Its 4.05% comparison is approximately relative superiority, not subtraction of percentage points (4.25). Source rounding is retained.

content.text: Accuracy ensures your attack lands as a clean hit negating a Block/Parry 1:1. If your Accuracy covers the exact amount of Block a target has, you will land 100% of your attacks.
There are diminishing returns to this stat
The average value of 100 Accuracy is roughly
If my Target has 2,000 Block and my Accuracy is 1,000 then he has a 60% ~ 70% chance to Parry
Parry is capped at an 80% chance and a difference of 1,200 is required to reach it
This allows us to calculate the  6% ~ 7% per 100 (6.66…%*1,200 = 80%)

The graph annotates X=1,200 at approximately 79%, while the prose calls a 1,200 difference the 80% cap. The “6.66…%*1,200 = 80%” line omits the per-100 scale; the curve is nonlinear, so the average is not a constant slope. No exact curve equation is given.
The graph below represents how the diminishing returns work for both Crit/Crit Resistance and Accuracy/Block
Critical Hit & Critical Resist use the same formula as Accuracy & Block/Parry which includes the 80% cap.
Refer to the graph and Accuracy explanation above

Skill passives are Additive so if your Critical Hit is 70% and you take a Skill passive that increases your Critical Hit by 30%, your Critical Hit % will be 80%. If you are hitting 80% Crit on a Skill you do
need to take a Crit increasing Specialty Perk

content.text: Defense reduces Damage taken by a %. Penetration subtracts directly from Defense. Penetration is overall a very low value stat due to how Defense works.

The headline says damage is reduced “by a %”, but the following examples subtract a fraction of the Defense value. Preserve the worked PVE and PVP outcomes rather than interpreting the headline as a separate multiplicative reduction.
In PVE, Damage will be reduced by 10% of your Defense value
In PVP, Damage will be reduced by 1% of your Defense value
Damage dealt is 500 with 100 penetration against a target with 200 defense
The Defense after Penetration is 100 (200 Defense - 100 Penetration)
500 - 10 = 490 Damage after Defense and Penetration calculations (499 for PVP)

title: Damage Tolerance Endurance and Combat Speed
summary: Damage Tolerance, Endurance probability, and source Combat Speed testing claims.
qualifiers: Source recommendations, first-person statements, and testing claims are Kanon’s. Figures are captured examples rather than universal costs or ideal builds.
Captured source update: 9/20/2026. Regional and unconfirmed details remain qualified as written.

Efficiency values assume an ideal KR end-game build at the start of Season 1, level 50 and Lava Heart armor, including support buffs. Global launch, future KR, class buffs and diminishing returns can change these values.

content.text: Damage Tolerance and Endurance are both highly effective Defensive stats. Damage Tolerance directly reduces Damage Boost against you while Endurance reduces your final damage taken by half.
The source later clarifies that the displayed Endurance percentage is the chance to take half damage, not a permanent halving of every hit.
All Damage Tolerance is a direct counter to its respective Damage Boost

In PVE Damage Tolerance, Boss Damage Tolerance, and PVE Damage Tolerance are the only ones of value considering Bosses do have Damage Boost (impossible to measure exactly how much due to damage being random)
Bosses do not have Front/Back Damage Boost, Weapon Damage Boost, Critical Hit, or Multi-hit meaning the respective Tolerance and Resistance against those stats are worthless
Endurance is only negated by Endurance Penetration. There is no Endurance Penetration from Bosses so whatever the % you see in your stat sheet will be the % chance you have to take 50% damage.

:  Combat Speed is a given S-tier individual stat that you stack as much as you can. This, however, is directly impacted by ping and FPS. When tested, a difference of 150-200 ping equated to roughly ≈  50% ~ 70% damage. Contrary to popular belief, there were no major differences between classes. Templar, Brawler, and Assassin were the three classes tested and were roughly similar. Spiritmaster may be an outlier due to the passive pet damage

Boss resistance and tolerance assertions and the ping/FPS damage comparison are attributed source claims, with the named tested classes and possible Spiritmaster exception retained. They are not universal measured constants.
